ELM Cleaning surfaces trust signals directly in its meta description ('Fully insured, police-checked and backed by a 24-hour re-clean') — the client should surface its $10m public liability insurance and vetted-team credentials just as prominently

Marketplace aggregators (Airtasker, hipages, Oneflare, ServiceSeeking) occupy several organic positions for this keyword, meaning the client's owned page is competing against high-authority directories, not just other local cleaners — differentiation on service quality and membership model matters more here than on lower-competition suburbs

ELM Cleaning explicitly references Hampton's bayside/foreshore geography ('apartments along the bay', 'holiday-rental turnovers along the foreshore') — a legitimate, data-grounded local hook the client can adopt without fabricating suburb facts

Price-range transparency is rewarded in this SERP: ServiceSeeking's snippet leads with specific $ bands (hourly, weekly, bond clean) for Hampton — the client's fixed, all-inclusive membership pricing is a genuine differentiator worth stating plainly rather than hiding behind a 'request a quote' only CTA
